title: On this view there is no difficulty in reconciling concurrence with freedom
source_text: III. Porro juxta hos Doctores nulla est difficultas in conciliando divino concursu cum libertate actuum humanorum, quandoquidem Deus ad illos immediate non concurrit, sed mediate tantum per liberum arbitrium quod semel creavit & perpetuo conservat.
pass_a_gloss: Further according to these Doctors there is no difficulty in reconciling the divine concurrence with the liberty of human acts, since God does not concur to them immediately, but mediately only through the free choice which he once created and perpetually preserves.
pass_b_english: For these teachers, then, reconciling God's concurrence with the freedom of human acts poses no problem at all.
God does not concur in those acts immediately, but only mediately, through the free choice he created once and keeps in being without interruption.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
